(https://www.governor.ny.gov/news/governor-hochul-announces-5-million-grants-awarded-help-pro-housing-communities-boost-housing)
[digital] Empire AI: created the consortium in FY25 and signed FY26 budget legislation expanding it — $90M additional capital (matched by $50M private and $25M SUNY), new members, alongside 'nation-leading AI protections'; earlier launched the $40M Empire AI beta supercomputer. (https://www.governor.ny.gov/news/governor-hochul-signs-legislation-expanding-historic-empire-ai-consortium-and-establishing)
[digital] Statewide DMV modernization contract with Fast Enterprises to replace systems more than 50 years old; also proposed a state Innovation Office, cyber incident reporting mandate, and AI training for the state workforce in her 2025 tech agenda. (https://statescoop.com/new-york-statewide-dmv-upgrade-hochul/)
[performance] Launched New York State's first Customer Experience strategy ('The New York Experience') to streamline processes and cut wait times across DOH, DMV and DOL using human-centered design; appointed Tonya Webster as the state's first Chief Customer Experience Officer. (https://www.governor.ny.gov/news/governor-hochul-announces-launch-new-york-states-first-customer-experience-strategy-improve)

candidates.name: Bruce Blakeman
candidates.notes:
GOP-designated nominee, also endorsed by the Conservative Party and President Trump; running mate Sheriff Todd Hood
[regulatory] Vows on Day One to scrap the CLCPA climate law's mandates (a 'utility bill bomb'), return $2B in unspent NYSERDA funds to ratepayers, cut utility taxes and hidden fees, and expand natural gas/nuclear supply — framing state energy mandates as cost-raising regulatory overreach. (https://southshorepress.com/stories/680291915-blakeman-vows-to-scrap-clcpa-slash-utility-bills)
[regulatory] Opposes the RAPID Act's state-level override of local permitting for large energy projects; campaigns on restoring local control over energy-project siting and against 'Albany mandates'. (https://spectrumlocalnews.com/nys/central-ny/politics/2026/04/16/rapid-act-clcpa)
[workforce] Government-workforce record centers on public-safety staffing: hired 600+ police/law enforcement officers as Nassau County Executive; touts flat property and sales taxes and eliminating $150M in scheduled tax hikes. No specific civil-service, merit-system, or state-union platform found. (https://www.blakemanfornewyork.com/)

candidates.name: Antonio Delgado
candidates.notes: former U.S. Representative — withdrew his primary challenge Feb 10, 2026 after failing to qualify at the Democratic convention

candidates.name: Vivek Ramaswamy
candidates.notes:
former federal DOGE co-lead designate; 2024 presidential candidate; running mate Ohio Senate President Rob McColley
Won GOP primary 82.5%-17.5% over Casey Putsch; Trump- and DeWine-endorsed
[regulatory] Pledge to 'shred every excess regulation' with a 10-for-1 rescission rule ('for every regulation we pass, we will require that at least 10 regulations are rescinded'), plus broad deregulation tied to zeroing out the state income tax. (https://www.courthousenews.com/vivek-ramaswamy-spins-quick-exit-from-trump-administration-into-run-for-ohio-governor/)
[workforce] Wants Ohio to be the first state with merit-based pay for teachers, principals, and administrators — explicitly willing to override collective bargaining agreements with public-sector unions; frames it as 'meritocracy in compensation' for the public workforce. (https://signalcleveland.org/vivek-ramaswamy-revives-merit-pay-teacher-debate-in-ohio/)
[digital] Economic pitch centers on an aggressive statewide AI data-center buildout ('Ohio River Valley as the next Silicon Valley'), streamlining energy permits and using JobsOhio, the Power Siting Board and PUCO to accelerate it; no specific state IT/AI-in-government plan found. (https://tiffinohio.net/posts/ramaswamy-data-center-expansion-ohio-governor/)
[performance] Emphasizes consolidating government spending and transparency as the path to zero income tax; announced a 'Crush Medicaid Waste, Fraud and Abuse' plan (May 2026) — DOGE-style efficiency framing carried from his federal role. (https://local12.com/news/local/republican-gubernatorial-candidate-vivek-ramaswamy-2026-ohio-governor-race-politics-election-economy-education-government-spending-transparency)

candidates.name: Amy Acton
candidates.notes:
former Director of the Ohio Department of Health (led Ohio's COVID-19 response); running mate David Pepper, former Ohio Democratic Party chair
Won Democratic primary unopposed
[performance] 'Cleaning Up Corruption' plank: mandate transparency and disclosure, open state bidding/contracting/appointments to public scrutiny, and shift state government culture to reward 'good work and merit' rather than 'deep pockets and big checkbooks.' (https://actonforgovernor.com/issue/cleaning-up-corruption/)
[workforce] 'Standing Up for Workers' plank: defend unions and collective bargaining against SB5-style attacks (implicitly covering public employees), oppose right-to-work, combat wage theft, and expand worker training and apprenticeships. (https://actonforgovernor.com/issue/standing-up-for-workers/)

candidates.name: Gentner Drummond
candidates.notes:
[regulatory] Campaign issues page pledges to 'cut red tape that slows down critical infrastructure and job-creating projects' and to cut healthcare red tape; no explicit position found on DOGE-OK's future or occupational licensing. (https://drummondok.com/issues/)
[performance] Pledges to 'end insider deals and wasteful spending' and 'strengthen transparency across state government'; no detailed KPI or performance-budgeting framework published. (https://drummondok.com/issues/)
[performance] As AG (April 2026), requested an independent state audit of the Oklahoma Health Care Authority over Medicaid spending concerns — agency-accountability track record rather than campaign plank. (https://oklahoma.gov/oag/news/newsroom/2026/april/drummond-requests-state-audit-of-oklahoma-health-care-authority.html)

candidates.name: Mike Mazzei
candidates.notes:
former Secretary of Budget under Gov. Stitt (2019-2020); Trump-endorsed
[regulatory] 'The Plan' pledges to streamline state licensing and permitting, sunset outdated regulations, and stand up a dedicated government-efficiency (DOGE-style) unit reviewing 'every agency, program, and line item — identifying duplication, mission creep, and outdated spending.' (https://mikeforok.com/the-plan/)
[performance] Results-based budgeting: 'No more blank checks. Every agency must prove it delivers value before receiving increases. Budgets will be performance-based, and results made public'; performance audits required by statute and mandatory sunset provisions on all new programs. (https://mikeforok.com/the-plan/)
[workforce] Proposes tying higher teacher compensation to performance and offering counties 401(k)-style retirement plans (explicitly not touching existing state retirement systems); message emphasizes 'cutting waste, demanding accountability from agencies, and measuring success.' (https://mikeforok.com/the-plan/)

candidates.name: Cyndi Munson
candidates.role: Oklahoma House Minority Leader (state representative, HD-85, since 2015)
candidates.notes:
[workforce] Priorities page pledges to raise public school funding above the regional average and deliver a pay raise to public school teachers and staff (public-sector workforce focus). (https://www.cyndimunson.com/Priorities)
[performance] Served on the Oversight Committee for the Legislative Office of Fiscal Transparency (LOFT), Oklahoma's agency performance/fiscal oversight body — track-record signal; no explicit KPI plank on campaign site. (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cyndi_Munson)

candidates.name: Tina Kotek
candidates.role: Governor of Oregon (since 2023); former Oregon House Speaker
candidates.notes:
[performance] Signed EO 23-04 on her first full day setting a KPI-style statewide housing production target of 36,000 homes/year (80% above trend) and creating the Housing Production Advisory Council; administration publicly tracks progress. (https://www.oregon.gov/gov/policies/pages/housing-production-advisory-council.aspx)
[performance] Reports semi-annual progress against her housing production goal (~50K units in the pipeline though most unrealized), an explicit outcomes/targets governance approach she says she will continue in a second term. (https://www.kgw.com/article/news/state/governor-kotek-oregon-state-housing-construction-goal-production/283-6abd5e4e-2f0b-42a0-9b45-e37cf02c0545)
[regulatory] Signed HB 2258 (July 2025) and a housing-supply package streamlining permitting: lets the Land Conservation and Development Commission and DCBS pre-approve housing plans and set statewide standards developers can use for fast-track approval. (https://oregoncapitalchronicle.com/2025/07/29/gov-kotek-signs-laws-to-boost-housing-supply-but-more-work-to-be-done-to-solve-crisis/)
[digital] Issued EO 23-26 creating the State Government AI Advisory Council for ethical AI use in state agencies; announced the resulting statewide AI Action Plan (Feb 2025) with five executive actions on AI governance, security, privacy, and workforce readiness. (https://www.oregon.gov/gov/eo/eo-23-26.pdf)
[digital] Oregon began rolling out AI training for state employees (July 2025) under the AI Action Plan implementation. (https://www.opb.org/article/2025/07/15/oregon-state-employees-ai-artificial-intelligence-training/)
[workforce] Issued a pro-union executive order requiring project labor agreements on large state construction projects — a strong organized-labor alignment signal — which a judge ruled illegal in March 2026; construction and public-sector unions are core re-election endorsers. (https://www.opb.org/article/2026/03/12/oregon-gov-kotek-order-union-work-projects-ruling-illegal/)

candidates.name: Christine Drazan
candidates.notes:
former Oregon House Republican Leader; 2022 GOP gubernatorial nominee
[regulatory] Platform blames 'red tape in Salem' and outdated forest management policies for the housing shortage and pledges to eliminate bureaucratic obstacles; core message that 'government needs to get out of the way'. (https://www.christinefororegon.com/)
[regulatory] At her campaign launch, called for state leaders to cut taxes and regulations ('We can get government out of the way'), framing housing, addiction, and cost-of-living problems as failures of over-regulation. (https://www.opb.org/article/2025/10/27/christine-drazan-oregon-governor-politics-tina-kotek-republican-leader/)
[performance] Government-efficiency/accountability plank: notes the state budget 'doubled in just a decade,' pledges government will 'tighten its belt,' and criticizes leaders for failing to spend taxpayer dollars efficiently on transportation, behavioral health, and housing. (https://www.christinefororegon.com/)

candidates.name: Josh Shapiro
candidates.role: Governor of Pennsylvania (first term since January 2023)
candidates.notes:
[workforce] First executive order (EO 2023-03) removed four-year degree requirements for 92% of commonwealth jobs (~65,000 positions), emphasizing skills-based hiring; administration reports hiring times reduced 32% and nearly 600 previously vacant permitting/licensing/certification jobs filled. (https://www.pa.gov/agencies/oa/newsroom/governor-shapiro-signs-first-executive-order-announcing-92-percent-of-commonwealth-jobs-do-not-require-a-four-year-degree)
[workforce] Follow-on EO 2025-01 targets critical state vacancies by recruiting experienced former federal employees into civil engineering, nursing, corrections, and accounting. (https://www.pa.gov/governor/newsroom/2025-press-releases/gov-shapiro-signs-executive-order-to-fill-critical-public-servic)
[regulatory] First-in-the-nation PAyback online money-back guarantee (permit/license/certification fees refunded if agencies miss deadlines); 40M+ applications processed since 2023 with only five refunds issued; eliminated a 15-year DEP permit backlog; permitting reform continued in his 2026-27 budget. (https://www.pa.gov/governor/newsroom/press-releases/governor-shapiro-launches-first-in-the-nation-online-money-back-)
[regulatory] DEP's SPEED program (launched 2025) lets applicants use DEP-verified third-party professionals for initial environmental permit reviews to cut time-to-issuance. (https://www.mankogold.com/publications-Shapiro-SPEED-PAyback-RGGI-PRESS.html)
[digital] First-in-the-nation generative AI pilot with OpenAI (ChatGPT Enterprise): 175 employees across 14 agencies averaged ~95 minutes/day saved; Phase 2 expanded generative AI tools to 3,000+ employees across 35 agencies. (https://statescoop.com/pennsylvania-expands-generative-ai-tools-3000-employees/)
[digital] CODE PA (Commonwealth Office of Digital Experience) reports $10M saved in three years via in-house digital delivery; 2026-27 budget adds $3.7M for CODE PA to modernize permitting/licensing platforms; new executive director Sara Hall appointed Feb 2026. (https://www.pa.gov/agencies/oa/newsroom/governor-shapiro-s-2025-26-budget-invests-in-code-pa-to-continue)
[performance] Reelection campaign built around his 'GSD' (Get Stuff Done) results record — executive delivery, permitting speed, a growing state economy — signaling a second-term agenda focused on government execution plus lowering housing and energy costs. (https://www.pbs.org/newshour/nation/josh-shapiro-running-for-2nd-term-as-pennsylvania-governor-trailed-by-talk-of-2028-white-house-bid)
[performance] Office of Transformation and Opportunity publicly reports faster permitting outcomes; 'Getting IT Done' reporting claims technology investments yielded millions in savings — outcome-tracking used as a governing and campaign asset. (https://riverreporter.com/stories/shapiro-admin-boasts-faster-permitting-through-pa-office-of-transformation-and-opportunity,240250)

candidates.name: Stacy Garrity
candidates.role: Pennsylvania State Treasurer (since January 2021); U.S. Army Reserve veteran
candidates.notes:
[digital] Proposes creating a state Office of Innovation tasked with finding where technology and AI can make state agencies more efficient (Pennsylvania Press Club speech). (https://www.spotlightpa.org/news/2026/04/pennsylvania-primary-election-stacy-garrity-governor-guide-elections/)
[performance] Runs on her Treasury record of saving taxpayers nearly $200 million by eliminating fraud and inefficiency; campaign message centers on government efficiency and holding the line on taxes. (https://www.spotlightpa.org/news/2026/04/pennsylvania-primary-election-stacy-garrity-governor-guide-elections/)

candidates.name: Daniel J. McKee
candidates.role: Governor of Rhode Island (since 2021); running for re-election
candidates.notes:
[performance] Learn365RI is his flagship outcomes push tied to the RI 2030 goal of matching/beating Massachusetts education outcomes by 2030; cites a 34% reduction in the RICAS ELA gap with MA, 18% in math, and 244,000 fewer student absences; pressing for continued Learn365RI funding in his FY27 budget. (https://governor.ri.gov/press-releases/governor-mckee-reinforces-need-fy-27-budget-investment-learn365ri-out-school)
[performance] RI 2030 statewide goals framework sets numeric 2030 targets (e.g., 49% of students meeting expectations in ELA, 47% in math) tracked at state and district level. (https://rhodeisland2030.ri.gov/ri-2030-priorities/strengthening-k-12-education/road-ri-2030-k-12-education-goals)
[digital] Signed EO 24-06 establishing a state AI Task Force (chaired by former Rep. Jim Langevin), an AI Center of Excellence under the Department of Administration, a Data Center of Excellence, and a chief data officer role; the Jan 2026 task force report calls for AI-automated citizen interactions, records modernization, and predictive analytics in state operations. (https://governor.ri.gov/press-releases/governor-mckee-signs-executive-order-establishing-artificial-intelligence-task-force)
[regulatory] Signed housing legislative packages that 'streamline production and cut through red tape,' including electronic building permitting for municipalities and codifying the State Building Code Office for uniform statewide code interpretation; RI's Office of Regulatory Reform continues review of executive-branch regulations. (https://governor.ri.gov/press-releases/governor-mckee-signs-housing-legislative-package-law)

candidates.name: Helena Buonanno Foulkes
candidates.notes:
2022 gubernatorial primary runner-up; leading McKee in 2026 primary polls (UNH July 2026: ~42-22), endorsed by AG Peter Neronha and 13 local Democratic committees
[performance] Core campaign frame is managerial competence ('Competence. Courage. Caring.'): Rhode Island 'spends more per person than surrounding states, and gets worse results' — an explicit spending-vs-outcomes efficiency argument drawn from her CVS management background. (https://helenafoulkes.com/)
[performance] RIDOT reform plan ('Never Again') responding to the Washington Bridge failure: create an Office of Safety and Accountability and rebuild in-house engineering expertise, prioritizing taxpayer interests over contractor profits. (https://helenafoulkes.com/reformdot)
[regulatory] Rhode Home housing plan pledges 'less red tape' and a $1B revolving loan fund to carry developers through permitting uncertainty and speed approvals, targeting 20,000 new homes over eight years. (https://www.oceanstatemedia.org/housing/housing-is-a-top-issue-in-the-governors-race-mckee-and-foulkes-have-different-plans)
[performance] Ethics/insider-reform plan 'You Shouldn't Have to Know a Guy' aimed at making the State House 'work for all Rhode Islanders, not just the insiders'. (https://helenafoulkes.com/knowaguy)

candidates.name: Aaron Guckian
candidates.role: Executive director, Rhode Island Dental Association
candidates.notes:
former aide to Gov. Don Carcieri; 2022 GOP nominee for lieutenant governor; won the RI GOP convention endorsement June 25, 2026
[workforce] 'Rhode Island Works Smarter' plan centers on partnering directly with frontline and union state workers: a 24/7 anonymous idea portal for employee suggestions and financial incentives for workers whose ideas produce savings — efficiency gains shared with employees rather than top-down cuts. (https://www.oceanstatemedia.org/politics/gop-candidate-for-governor-aaron-guckian-on-state-spending-education-and-the-path-to-becoming-governor)
[performance] Targets nearly $600 million in state consultant spending within the $15.2B budget, proposing to 'work directly with Rhode Island talent and start to get leaner,' with savings routed to lower taxes and fees; describes the approach as continuous 'process improvement'. (https://www.oceanstatemedia.org/politics/gop-candidate-for-governor-aaron-guckian-on-state-spending-education-and-the-path-to-becoming-governor)
[digital] Says the Works Smarter savings model should be 'powered by modern technology,' including using technology to eliminate administrative paperwork burdens on teachers and modernize testing. (https://www.oceanstatemedia.org/politics/gop-candidate-for-governor-aaron-guckian-on-state-spending-education-and-the-path-to-becoming-governor)

candidates.name: Robert Raimondo
candidates.notes: announced January 2026 on a pledge to eliminate the state income tax; running in the Sept 8 GOP primary against party-endorsed Guckian

candidates.name: Ken Block
candidates.notes: Moderate Party founder; two-time gubernatorial candidate; declared independent candidate for the November 2026 general election

candidates.name: Alan Wilson
candidates.notes:
Won the June 23 Republican runoff with 68.6% over Pamela Evette
[regulatory] Pledges to 'DOGE South Carolina government from top to bottom,' cut taxes and slash red tape; has proposed reforming the State Inspector General's office into South Carolina's version of DOGE. (https://www.foxnews.com/politics/south-carolina-ag-mounts-gubernatorial-bid-advocates-abolishing-state-income-tax-doge-ing-government)
[regulatory] Authored 'Let's Bring DOGE To South Carolina' op-ed calling for a state-level government efficiency initiative to root out waste, fraud, and abuse. (https://www.fitsnews.com/2025/02/14/alan-wilson-lets-bring-doge-to-south-carolina/)
[performance] 'Families First Audit Initiative': comprehensive audits of state and local government with savings returned to taxpayers; pledges to modernize the DOT, streamline project timelines, and ensure 'every dollar in the state budget delivers value.' (https://wilsonforsc.com/priorities/)
[digital] As AG, active on AI governance rather than gov-IT modernization: opposed a federal 10-year preemption of state AI laws as 'federal overreach' and led 44 AGs warning Big Tech over AI risks to children; no campaign plank found on state IT modernization or AI in government operations. (https://www.scag.gov/about-the-office/news/attorney-general-alan-wilson-fights-back-federal-proposal-to-strip-states-of-authority-over-ai/)

candidates.name: Jermaine Johnson
candidates.notes:
Won the June 9 Democratic primary outright with 58.2% over Billy Webster and Mullins McLeod
[workforce] Pro-labor workforce agenda: create a labor advisory council to recommend a state minimum wage, remove barriers to employment, combat wage theft; raise salaries for and hire additional state and local law enforcement; endorsed by the SC AFL-CIO. (https://www.wsoctv.com/news/local/political-beat-candidate-guide-south-carolina-governor-d/HH2M7VTXGVH3VI5YLBS4PN36CE/)
[performance] Proposes a full audit of South Carolina's public education system to increase access and quality; campaign framed around 'Accountability, Integrity, and Commitment,' though the audit plank is education-specific rather than government-wide. (https://johnsonforsc.com/policies)
[regulatory] Limited signal: labor advisory council would be tasked with 'removing certain barriers to employment' (adjacent to occupational-licensing reform); no broader red-tape/permitting or DOGE-style plank found. (https://johnsonforsc.com/policies)

candidates.name: Larry Rhoden
candidates.role: Incumbent Governor of South Dakota (elevated from Lt. Governor Jan 2025 when Kristi Noem resigned
candidates.notes:
seeking first full term)
[regulatory/permitting reform & procedure] Signed SB 133, a REINS Act-style law imposing legislative checks on the administrative state: any proposed regulation with compliance/implementation costs over $3 million across two years requires additional scrutiny and approval from the legislature. (https://www.goldwaterinstitute.org/south-dakota-reins-in-regulations/)
[regulatory reform / red tape] Frames cutting red tape as a core governing philosophy — 'not about more government or more red tape' — emphasizing reduced regulatory burden so businesses can operate without government interference. (https://www.nssf.org/articles/nssf-profile-qa-governor-larry-rhoden-r-s-d/)

candidates.name: Toby Doeden
candidates.role: Aberdeen businessman (retail and real estate executive; political newcomer)
candidates.notes:
[regulatory reform & government efficiency] Pledged to create a 'South Dakota Department of Government Efficiency,' audit every state agency, publicly release 'every line item' of state spending, and eliminate 'waste, inefficiencies and redundancies' to fund phasing out property taxes. (https://southdakotasearchlight.com/2025/05/28/doeden-joins-race-for-governor-with-pledge-to-eliminate-property-taxes/)
[performance/outcomes management (spending transparency)] Says he will 'lower the overhead' and 'get rid of the fat and the pork' via agency-by-agency audits with publicly released line-item spending; critics note he has not named specific replacement revenue streams. (https://www.mitchellrepublic.com/news/local/governors-race-doeden-aims-to-slash-taxes-increase-revenue-as-governor)

candidates.name: Dan Ahlers
candidates.role: Executive Director of the South Dakota Democratic Party
candidates.notes:
former state legislator and small business owner; 2020 U.S. Senate nominee
[digital government / connectivity] Platform centers on infrastructure investment including expansion of rural broadband access, citing digital connectivity as a significant barrier across the state; also campaigns on government transparency. (https://politics-government.news-articles.net/content/2026/02/17/ahlers-exceeds-expectations-leads-in-south-dakota-governorship-race.html)

candidates.name: Marsha Blackburn
candidates.notes:
[performance/outcomes management & government efficiency] Campaign issues page pledges to evaluate 'even the most conservative state governments, including Tennessee, for opportunities to modernize, save taxpayer money, reduce fraud, and cut waste.' (https://marshablackburn.com/issues/cutting-wasteful-government-spending/)
[civil service & workforce] In the Senate introduced the 'DOGE Acts': federal hiring/salary freeze, 5% workforce cut over three years, a pilot for merit-based (not seniority-based) pay (Federal Employee Performance and Accountability Act), the SHOW UP Act ending expanded telework, and agency relocation out of D.C. — indicative of her workforce-management approach. (https://www.blackburn.senate.gov/2025/2/issues/jobs-and-economy/blackburn-introduces-doge-acts-to-make-federal-government-more-efficient-and-slash-wasteful-spending)
[AI / digital government] Unveiled a national AI policy framework (the 'TRUMP AMERICA AI Act') for a single federal rulebook; earlier led the successful effort to strip the federal AI moratorium from the One Big Beautiful Bill Act, preserving states' (incl. Tennessee's) authority to regulate AI harms. (https://www.blackburn.senate.gov/2025/12/technology/blackburn-unveils-national-policy-framework-for-artificial-intelligence)

candidates.name: John Rose
candidates.role: U.S. Representative, TN-6 (2019-present); farmer and businessman
candidates.notes:
[regulatory/permitting reform & red tape] Campaign pledges to 'make Tennessee the most business-friendly state in the country by cutting job-killing red tape for entrepreneurs, farmers, and small business owners.' (https://johnrose.com/issues/)
[regulatory reform (federal record)] In Congress has focused on 'reducing burdensome federal regulations on individuals, families, businesses, and community banks' via House Financial Services Committee work; runs on his CEO/business background as a management credential. (https://johnrose.house.gov/about)

candidates.name: Monty Fritts
candidates.notes: [government efficiency / size of government] Campaign slogan 'Liberty & Less Government'; argues Tennessee's state budget grew 59% in six years under Gov. Lee and pledges to shrink state government. (https://tennesseelookout.com/2025/09/08/east-tennessee-republican-runs-for-governor-to-topple-nashville-establishment/)

candidates.name: Jerri Green
candidates.notes:
[performance/outcomes management & transparency] Plans an online public 'Report Card' letting Tennesseans track state contracts and grants in plain language — where the money goes, what it is supposed to deliver, and whether it actually does. (https://greenforgovernor.com/policy/)
[state workforce / appointments] Pledges to appoint 'qualified, ethical leaders — not political cronies' to run state agencies; Day One Plan also includes ending private prison contracts. (https://greenforgovernor.com/policy/)

candidates.name: Kevin Lee McCants
candidates.role: Pastor; former production supervisor; 2024 U.S. Senate candidate

candidates.name: Greg Abbott
candidates.role: Governor of Texas (incumbent since 2015), seeking a fourth term
candidates.notes:
[regulatory/permitting reform & government efficiency] Signed SB 14 (April 2025) creating the Texas Regulatory Efficiency Office ('Texas DOGE') to help agencies identify unnecessary rules and streamline the regulatory process; in its first reviews TREO recommended 435+ regulations for amendment or repeal across 11 agencies (~$123M estimated savings), with its public website launched May 2026. (https://gov.texas.gov/news/post/governor-abbott-signs-texas-doge-into-law-at-texas-capitol)
[regulatory efficiency implementation] Texas Regulatory Efficiency Office staffed with a first director and up to 18 FTEs at $22.8M over five years; tasked with stricter cost standards for new regulations and checking growth of the administrative state. (https://www.govtech.com/workforce/texas-regulatory-efficiency-office-gets-its-first-director)
[AI in government / AI governance] Signed HB 149, the Texas Responsible Artificial Intelligence Governance Act (TRAIGA), June 2025 (effective Jan 1, 2026), making Texas the third state with a comprehensive AI law; intent-based liability framework with safe harbors for entities substantially complying with the NIST AI Risk Management Framework. (https://iapp.org/news/a/governor-signs-texas-responsible-artificial-intelligence-governance-act)
[performance-based pay / public workforce incentives] Expanded merit-based Teacher Incentive Allotment under HB 2 (~$4B for teacher pay raises); announced $750M in TIA awards to 65,000+ teachers across 800+ school systems in 2025-26, with a path to six-figure salaries for top-rated teachers. (https://gov.texas.gov/news/post/governor-abbott-announces-750-million-in-teacher-incentive-allotment-awards)

candidates.name: Gina Hinojosa
candidates.role: Texas State Representative, District 49 (Austin), serving since 2017
candidates.notes:
[state workforce / public-sector pay and unions] Campaign priorities pledge to fight 'alongside union teachers,' invest in teacher pay, and protect the Teacher Retirement System from voucher-driven funding drains; frames public-workforce investment as part of an anti-privatization education agenda. (https://ginafortexas.com/priorities/)
[accountability / anti-corruption in government] Emphasizes holding officials accountable for how tax dollars are spent; no specific published plans found on regulatory/permitting reform, digital government/IT modernization, or KPI-based performance management. (https://ginafortexas.com/about/)

candidates.name: Pat Dixon
candidates.role: Former Lago Vista city council member (two terms)
candidates.notes: former chair of the Libertarian Party of Texas

candidates.name: Phil Scott
candidates.notes:
announced May 28, 2026 he is seeking a sixth two-year term (confirmed running)
[regulatory/permitting reform] January 2026 budget address called for regulatory reforms to increase housing development: modernizing Act 250, extending interim housing exemptions to 2030, adjusting exemption requirements, repealing the 'Road Rule' (https://www.wamc.org/news/2026-02-05/vermont-governor-calls-for-regulatory-reforms-to-help-increase-housing-development)
[regulatory/permitting reform] Signed 'historic' housing legislation (S.100 HOME Act) and Act 181's shift to location-based Act 250 jurisdiction with a professionalized Land Use Review Board; pushing 2026 Legislature to go further on housing (https://governor.vermont.gov/press-release/governor-phil-scott-signs-historic-housing-legislation-law)
[performance & outcomes management] 2026 State of the State centered on implementing Act 73 education transformation — foundation funding formula 'proven to produce better outcomes,' governance consolidation, spending curbs through 2029 — his signature next-term delivery agenda (https://www.vermontpublic.org/local-news/2026-01-07/gov-phil-scott-insists-on-lawmakers-keeping-our-word-on-education-reform-in-state-of-state-speech)
[digital government / AI] Agency of Digital Services deployed ChatVT, a homemade AI chatbot for all state employees (early 2025), building on Vermont being first in the nation with a state AI director and AI council (Act 132 of 2022) (https://vtdigger.org/2025/05/22/final-reading-meet-chatvt-the-state-of-vermonts-homemade-ai-chatbot/)
[digital government / IT modernization] New advisory body created May 2026 to recommend how Vermont government and businesses could adopt AI; lawmakers scrutinizing the administration's $70M state IT modernization program after a postponed rollout in April 2026 (https://vtdigger.org/2026/05/19/a-new-body-will-recommend-how-state-government-and-vermont-businesses-could-adopt-ai/)
[civil service & state workforce] His August 2025 'Hybrid Work Standard' (3 in-office days/week) was overturned by the Vermont Labor Relations Board in April 2026 for refusing to bargain in good faith with VSEA; union cited 77% vacancy rate at Waterbury State Office Complex (https://vtdigger.org/2026/04/01/vermont-labor-board-says-state-must-end-return-to-office-requirement-for-employees/)

candidates.name: Amanda Janoo
candidates.notes:
co-founder of Wellbeing Economy Alliance of Vermont, former UN economic policy advisor; first Democrat to enter (March 10, 2026)
[performance & outcomes management] 'Wellbeing economy' platform proposes a Vermont Future Generations Commissioner with tenure beyond political cycles to hold government to account; major policies and investments must show how they advance collectively-set goals, measured by wellbeing indicators rather than GDP (https://www.janooforvt.com/)
[performance & outcomes management] Career at Wellbeing Economy Alliance helped governments in Canada, New Zealand, and Wales evaluate economies by social and ecological wellbeing; proposes statewide strategic goals via participatory town-meeting-style process with investments evaluated against them (https://www.colchestersun.com/news/government/amanda-janoo-seeks-governorship-to-create-wellbeing-economy/article_a3e867d9-cc55-526f-965f-3145e8a99b11.html)

candidates.name: Aly Richards
candidates.role: Former CEO of Let's Grow Kids (2015-2025), the advocacy group behind Vermont's 2023 child care law (Act 76)
candidates.notes:
entered race April 6, 2026
[regulatory/permitting reform] Housing is her top priority: commits to 'set clear annual housing production targets by region' and 'make it easier and faster to build,' signaling permitting/production streamlining (no detailed Act 250 position) (https://alyforvt.com/platform/)
[performance & outcomes management] Platform emphasizes data-driven, outcomes-focused governance; pledges to ensure Act 76 child care benefits are 'working as intended with a continued commitment to accountability and tracking return on investment' (https://alyforvt.com/platform/)

candidates.name: Tom Tiffany
candidates.notes:
[regulatory-reform] Platform pledges to 'cut burdensome regulations to make housing, childcare, and healthcare more affordable'; as a state senator authored 2017 SB 288 on review/sunset reports for occupational licenses; June 2026 statewide ad buy highlights cutting red tape. (https://tomtiffany.com/solutions/)
[civil-service] Defends Act 10 (served in the Assembly when it passed): 'What Act 10 did is put elected officials in charge of their budget... an effort to strike a balance' — contrast with all Democratic candidates, who vow repeal. (https://www.wjfw.com/news/local/wisconsin-governor-candidates-speak-out-on-act-10-with-democrats-vowing-to-repeal-it/article_8fba2faf-4543-4187-8e97-10b5509c94b2.html)
[performance-management] Education plank stresses outcomes and accountability: 'higher academic standards and transparent reporting,' funding directed 'to students, teachers, and communities rather than bureaucracy,' rewarding successful schools. (https://tomtiffany.com/solutions/)

candidates.name: Sara Rodriguez
candidates.notes:
[digital-government] Dedicated issue plank 'Make AI Work for Wisconsin Workers': as governor she 'will ensure artificial intelligence creates opportunity for Wisconsin workers – not just profits for tech companies.' (https://www.saraforwi.com/issues)
[civil-service] Supports repealing Act 10 and restoring public-sector collective bargaining; endorsed by AFSCME. (https://www.wjfw.com/news/local/wisconsin-governor-candidates-speak-out-on-act-10-with-democrats-vowing-to-repeal-it/article_8fba2faf-4543-4187-8e97-10b5509c94b2.html)

candidates.name: David Crowley
candidates.notes: [civil-service] Platform includes 'Repealing Act 10 and restoring the collective bargaining rights for workers'; endorsed by the Professional Fire Fighters of Wisconsin; led Democratic field in fundraising ($800,949 in first filing period). (https://www.wjfw.com/news/local/wisconsin-governor-candidates-speak-out-on-act-10-with-democrats-vowing-to-repeal-it/article_8fba2faf-4543-4187-8e97-10b5509c94b2.html)

candidates.name: Mandela Barnes
candidates.role: Former Lieutenant Governor of Wisconsin (2019-2023); 2022 U.S. Senate nominee
candidates.notes: [civil-service] Supports repealing Act 10, framing the state as a model employer: 'the state has to lead by example by creating those workplaces where people are fairly compensated... repealing Act 10 is the first step to giving people that voice back.' (https://www.wjfw.com/news/local/wisconsin-governor-candidates-speak-out-on-act-10-with-democrats-vowing-to-repeal-it/article_8fba2faf-4543-4187-8e97-10b5509c94b2.html)

candidates.name: Francesca Hong
candidates.notes:
[civil-service] Most detailed labor/workforce plank in the field: 'nail the coffin of Act 10 shut,' enshrine a constitutional right for all workers to organize, repeal right-to-work, restore prevailing wage, and have state workers 'participate in executive decision-making.' (https://francescahong.com/policy/)
[performance-management] 'Cut contractor waste' plank: commission a study of government outsourcing to identify waste; pledges to properly staff agencies (e.g., DNR) to implement existing law. (https://francescahong.com/policy/)
[regulatory-reform] Narrow red-tape plank on health care access: 'Fran will cut the red tape by expanding reimbursement pathways' for opioid-use-disorder treatment. (https://francescahong.com/policy/)

candidates.name: Megan Degenfelder
candidates.notes:
former oil/gas and coal industry government affairs executive
[performance/outcomes management] At the June 2026 gubernatorial debate called for continuous performance auditing of state government: 'We should be auditing every single state agency, every single budget line all the time. Government is a beast, and you need someone in there who can tame it.' (https://oilcity.news/government/state/2026/06/01/megan-degenfelder-brent-bien-face-off-in-gubernatorial-campaign-debate/)
[regulatory/permitting reform] Pledges to 'reduce red tape' as governor; cites her record fighting federal regulatory burdens on Wyoming energy and wants federal grant money to flow to states and districts 'without the red tape.' Platform lists 'Limited & Transparent Government' as a core issue. (https://www.wyodaily.com/story/2026/06/25/news/governor-candidates-megan-degenfelder-republican/17964.html)
[digital government / modernization] Campaign priorities include 'promoting innovation in government and industry' and 'modernizing state government'; issues platform also includes a 'Digital Assets' plank. (https://www.yourwyominglink.com/news/politics/megan-degenfelder-emphasizes-leadership-experience-in-governor-bid/article_b6eba0b4-d35e-4bab-a091-3b7aff17480f.html)

candidates.name: Eric Barlow
candidates.notes:
former Speaker of the Wyoming House; rancher and veterinarian
[civil service & state workforce] Proposes five regional governor's offices staffed by hires from regional communities rather than centralized in Cheyenne, to improve communication and coordination on permitting, workforce, infrastructure, and local government needs. (https://www.codyenterprise.com/news/wyoming_news/article_d6ec45db-d71e-4bdd-91af-1f75b71b822e.html)
[regulatory/permitting reform] Touts legislative record cutting red tape in healthcare 'so providers can focus on patients, not paperwork'; frames his goal as limited government that 'delivers the services in a respectful and efficient manner and lives well within its means.' (https://www.barlowforwyo.com/positions)

candidates.name: Brent Bien
candidates.role: Retired U.S. Marine Corps colonel; 2022 gubernatorial candidate (Cody)
candidates.notes:
[performance/outcomes management] Pledges a full budgetary audit of Wyoming state government, noting 'this state has not done a full-blown budgetary audit since 1989. Whoever's belly-aching loudest is going to get audited first.' (https://oilcity.news/government/state/2026/06/01/megan-degenfelder-brent-bien-face-off-in-gubernatorial-campaign-debate/)
[regulatory/permitting reform] Strongly deregulatory: 'The only business that government has in business is simply to get out of the way. It's to cut taxes. It's to deregulate'; message centers on shrinking government. (https://brentbien.com/)

candidates.name: Kenneth R. Casner
candidates.role: Retired Army/Army National Guard veteran (27 years) from Elk Mountain
candidates.notes: third gubernatorial bid
